reviews.title: False Advertisement
reviews.text: This app is misleading, advertising to be entertaining and able to teach one a concept in depth. The app is useless if you have a clue about Ebooks, basic YouTube searches with college courseware, or even library access. It is almost entirely composed of AI generated script and art, yielding a diluted feeling at best. The novelty of learning new concepts is better captured by watching online lectures or reading a science article from a reproducible study. This app is sadly AI dogoop.

reviews.text: No mentira

reviews.title: It’s for little kids
reviews.text: This has to be a joke

reviews.title: I don’t feel smarter
reviews.text: So far it’s simple slides with a few sentence of content.

reviews.title: Kind of boring
reviews.text:
I have more than 10 years of conversations with many types of people related to P2P sales.

IMHO, I have some serious concerns about the unrealistic dialogue scenarios. I have big concerns about what the characters say and why, especially when compared to real-life situations. Sometimes, the purpose or context of a conversation is unclear. Are you trying to leave, or are you “flirting” on the way to live, but what for?

This app really doesn’t develop the skills I expected. Most of the material (around 90%) consists of audio/reading content rather than dialogue scripts, and much of it can be found online for free with the help of AI.

reviews.title: Yet another front end app for a cash cow
reviews.text: Start the app, answer a lot of questions, give your email address, then pay £60 to continue. - no thank you. How about a free demo period first to see if your content is worth the money? Absolutely sick of this front loading stuff.

reviews.title: Looks good but isn’t
reviews.text: Prompt after prompt to sign up for a paid subscription from the start. Do t bother.

reviews.title: SMC
reviews.text: There should be a “try before you buy period” to see if you like it. I’m not signing up for any App that has recurring charges, unless I’ve used it for a while and enjoyed it. For all I know, it’s loaded with information that’s not useful or relevant to my needs and intrusive ads.

reviews.title: J
reviews.text: Tried the electrics course. Information seemed AI generated and the imagery definitely was. Course was incredibly short. Finished 60% in less than a day. Not impressed

reviews.title: Poor ethics
reviews.text:
I tried this app a while ago and while it was briefly engaging the content was fairly basic and the interface a little slow. I stopped using it and deleted the app, not realising I had a subscription. I noticed when they charged me again without notifying me beforehand (I can’t stand that), and cancelled. When I went to cancel, they tried TWICE to keep me hooked by giving me first 50% and then 80% off.

My advice to future users: the app is ok for what it is, just remember you have a subscription, and threaten to leave them at least once per month to get more than 50% off.

reviews.title: Junk
reviews.text:
I got a real engineering degree in less time than it took me to fill out the survey questions you’re forced to fill out before actually using the app. Don’t waste your time here.

The developer responded to my honest review by claiming the answers to your questions determine the learning path. Here are just some of the questions they ask:

- Gender
- Age
- How we found you?
- Whether we’ve used other apps before
- Where do you get your information from (Google, websites, social media)
- Do you feel guilty about how you spend your time?
- Email?

I chose math learning path and was dumped into a course about engineering logic. 

I’d love for the developer to respond again and tell me how any of those questions affect the learning path and are more than just a blatant information grab they use to sell my psychographics to advertisers and data brokers. 

If I could give it zero stars, I would this is canned spam turned into an app.  Shame on Apple for allowing this garbage on their platform.

reviews.title: Clicked the free trail but it’s charged me £14.99..
reviews.text: Clicked on the free trial but not I’ve been charged £14.99.. I want my money back

reviews.title: Extra Charges with no warnings
reviews.text:
This app design is good and potentially very interesting but I signed up on a promotion for (I think) one month at £11.49 and I looked at by bank statement after 3 days of use and I've had two additional charges one of £7.59 and one of £14.99! Now I'm okay (from what I've seen so far with the idea of £11.49 per month but these additional charges need to be refunded as soon as possible.

Following the above I’ve had no contact from this App developer and the have charged me another £29.95 and £14.99 with no renewal notification. I’m considering if they do not repay all monies and cancelling my account taking this matter further. Ridiculous and sad considering the actual application is good but not worth these charges.

reviews.title: Terrible user flow
reviews.text:
I spent at least 5 minutes answering a survey riddled with advertisement of the app itself only to get to a point where I need to pay for a subscription before even seeing what the app is like?

They literally collect your email and have you sign terms of service and privacy policy before telling you the subscription price - scammy.

reviews.title: Didn’t get started
reviews.text:
The app kept crashing, I got up to selecting my gender…sorry “how I identify” 🙄
And it wouldn’t go any further.

reviews.title: Scam expensive
reviews.text: Goes through a long setup process then hits you with the ridiculous pricing structure!

reviews.title: No way to test game
reviews.text: Saw an ad for this app on Facebook, looked awesome, saw that it had really good ratings. But unfortunately there is a paywall to play the game, which is fine, I pay for apps all the time but I have no way of even testing the game to even see how it works or what it’s like whatsoever, horrible business model, definitely would suggest implementing some sort of way to actually play the game for a short period of time so people know what they are actually even buying, or showcasing the app in some way that shows how it works, zero information whatsoever just goes straight to asking for money. That’s a 1 star for me, I wish there was some way to know what it is that I’m purchasing, the ad looked really cool, but I have no clue. I’ve never bought a car without test driving it first.

reviews.title: Don’t bother
reviews.text: You have to go through a series of assessment questions which it then ignores before it tells you how much it costs. Don’t bother.

reviews.title: Mr
reviews.text:
First off, I’m not putting this app down but this is a chargeable app it’ll grab all your personal details and the. Say you need to pay, 
Secondly, I’m sure it’s a great app, but the £59 annual charge should be highlighted on the first slide. However interesting it is and as much as I’d enjoy this app, I deleted and unsubscribed instantly when I found out you need to pay

reviews.title: Paywall
reviews.text: I’m the customer, you need your customers to want to buy your product. If I can’t even try it without signing up to a subscription, I don’t want it. And a free trial doesn’t count. You should be able to use the app then decide if it’s something you want to sign up to. I’m not going to blindly sign up to an automatic subscription. 0 stars

reviews.title: Poor attention to detail
reviews.text:
I am interested in learning more about electricity. In the questions asked before lessons begin I indicated I prefer theory first yet when the actual subject education began it immediately started an interactive quiz (virtually wire an LED circuit). Problem is the light was an icon of an incandescent bulb - not an LED. I was confused since an incandescent bulb has no polarity. Then the lessons jumped to solving the resistance required to produce a current of 20 mA without any lesson about relationship between resistance, voltage, and current. 

I'm out $14 for a month since they didn't offer a trial. I now know why... they get at least $14 out of you before you realize what you're getting.

reviews.title: Not what I expected
reviews.text:
I was interested in this app because the marketing convinced me that it could help me work on my charisma, how to use my voice… and when I try the topic “speak eloquently and charismatically”, to my frustration, everything is just an AI voice reading text on the screen, with the intonation and cadence that doesn’t suit voice use examples or charisma training. when it was talking about the power of the intonation, it said “our team delivers results” about four times, and all four times should have sounded different, to showcase the changes in tone and cadence…. I’m not happy, I expected content created by real people, I was expecting those experts from Harvard and those other universities they boast about on their marketing, to narrate the contents, I hoped this app was not just more AI stuff!!
Even for the small talk training, there are AI pictures of people, and an instrumental music, but no people’s voices so that I can learn how to use intonation to say things in a funny way, or serious, flirty, etc.
ChatGPT or Gemini can do what this app does for free, with the right prompt! Come on!
I used it for about half an hour, and already want a refund!

reviews.title: Be Careful Of Your Payment
reviews.text:
Be careful with AI training apps when it comes to subscriptions and billing. I’ve had concerning experiences with more than one of them.

With SmartMeet, I clearly remember canceling my subscription, but later found that it appeared active again and I was charged. What makes this especially frustrating is that subscription changes have to be managed through their website rather than directly through Apple’s subscription settings. This makes it much harder to notice if anything changes with your subscription status.

Based on my experience, I strongly recommend taking screenshots of your purchase, subscription status, and cancellation confirmation whenever using apps like these. Keep your receipts and check your billing regularly.

reviews.title: Dont do it
reviews.text: I downloaded the app to check it out & paid the 1st month. I was very uninterested in its content. I then cancelled within a few days on April 20th & received a confirmation email back on April 20th that was cancelled. I check my account & see they have taken $25 out each month through August. I forwarded the confirmation email explaining this was cancelled in April & requested a refund for each month after -when they continued to charge me. They verified it was cancelled in time & told me that they would only be crediting August back.  They must have taken it a step further in the fine print that you must cancel in 2 separate places within the site. Very misleading

reviews.title: Do you actually care about this app and the customers? We will see in future updates
reviews.text: Not designed for people with any kind of learning difficulties or preference of learning style my. I have ADHD and extreme anxiety. I didn’t really excel in school because not only am I a visual learner. Meaning I need to watch a video or see someone doing something but the way that the information sticks and the way I’m able to build confidence. Is by doing what is being instructed hands on that way I can get realtime feedback,and ask questions that will help me improve. The other issue that I thought was absolutely crazy was on the lesson that talks about changing the pitch of how you’re speaking and not to sound monotone. The lady says to repeat a sentence and change the pitch of each word to see how it sounds so then she does it and there is literally no change. I thought maybe my phone was messed up or my ears had committed suicide. Nope no pitch changes.

reviews.title: This is a scam
reviews.text: This app has appeared as a purchase on my Apple App Store account. I did not access or purchase this app. I have never downloaded or opened app. It does not appear as downloaded on any of my devices. I did not consent to any payment being taken. Even so, the company has managed to take payment from my bank account. Beware - this is a scam. Apple - get your security sorted out! This is a breach.

reviews.title: Don't ask me how I identify!
reviews.text: I installed this app out of curiosity as I'm interested in learning about electrical engineering. I have just deleted it without even creating an account. Why? Because the very first question in the signup process is: "How do you identify?" I'm not trans or LGBTQ+, I am a man. A straight man. That's not" how I identify ", that's what I am. When the developer stops trying to railroad ordinary people down these woke paths I will consider subscribing.

reviews.title: Onboarding is terrible...
reviews.text:
Dude… the onboarding is awful. It’s just some goofy filler questions with a bunch of “hey, look at all the fake reviews we bought…” I mean it’s ridiculous. Just get with it…

I just go through the onboarding, well actually I might not even be done with it and it’s already prompting me with a rating and review, so here ya go. 

I hate apps that force that popup.. if you shove the ratings popup in my face before I even get to explore the app, you’re gonna get a 1 star. 

I’ll update this review if the app is actually good and turns out to be worth the time and effort to come back and update this review.. but if you’re reading this, then I most likely just uninstalled the app. So we’ll see..

Edit: just got asked YET AGAIN to rate it in the App Store after completing the VERY FIRST problem, but this time it was more of a heartfelt beg than the default one. If y’all would have just kept the second request and removed the first one, it wouldn’t be that bad. But don’t ask after the first problem. At least ask for reviews after maybe the third problem.

reviews.title: Totally disappointed
reviews.text: The advertisement promotes something completely fun, full of games as learning tools, just as shown in the ad — but in reality it’s only a theory‑based app. The moment you pay for the subscription, they already mislead you into purchasing additional content, and they took £40 from me. Absolutely disappointing.

reviews.title: Don’t believe the adds
reviews.text: When you see the advert it shows interactive games that indicate will make you a savant of electrical engineering or whatever subject you choose. The reality is it’s a series of bullet points that gives you a highly condensed summary of a subject and the games are essentially a digital pin the tail on the donkey. The timers don’t seem to correlate to actual time spent on a subject to the point I got so bored I started skipping and ultimately cancelling. The adds indicated learning through interaction but it’s quite far detached from that.

reviews.title: Unresponsive to subscription enquiries and app issues
reviews.text:
Numerous emails to their support address regarding an incorrect subscription status in the app and web app have since gone silent. They are either incabable of resolving this technical glitch, or unwilling. Either way, I’m not confident of cancelling the reduced price trial subscription when the time comes - so would advise all others to avoid this app should they also fall foul.

I had high hopes to make my procrastination time productive, but am left disappointed instead.

Follow up note: Their ‘Head of Customer Service” thinks it’s acceptable to put the blame on me for expecting a response within four days - after radio silence beforehand. I suggest they go back to customer service school or choose another profession. I would take 2 additional stars off this review by your ‘service’. 

Having said that, those responsible for enacting the refund, did so quickly, with respect, professionalism and dignity toward me. From your actions, you gain the extra 2 stars back - so back to 1 star.

reviews.title: This app will truly screw up your life for a couple weeks!
reviews.text: Once you decide to pay for the trial of this app, it’s going to flag any credit or debit card as a fraud! This will end up leaving you to wait for a new card for a couple weeks. Within those couple of weeks they are going to completely expire your subscription. During that time you will not be able to use this app or your card because you are waiting for a new one to come in! This app will totally screw up your life for a few weeks! The lessons it has in it are great. But the time it takes to get your life back on track is completely screwed.

reviews.title: DECEPTIVE "Guarantee" — Read the fine print before you pay!
reviews.text:
Be warned: SmartyMe’s "30-Day Money-Back Guarantee" is a total trap. They advertise a guarantee to get you to subscribe, but their terms and conditions make it almost impossible to actually get a refund.
To qualify, you are forced to use the app for at least 150 minutes in the first month. If you realize the app is low quality after 10 minutes and want out, they will DENY your refund because you didn't "use it enough." This is a predatory tactic designed to keep your money regardless of your satisfaction. It is a "dark pattern" intended to trick consumers. Save your money and find a more transparent app.

reviews.title: Cost isn’t spelled out
reviews.text:
I had to spend 5 min answering a bunch of questions just for it to tell me there’s a cost to the app. I don’t see any indication that this app cost money or has in app purchases upfront in the App Store. This review is solely based on the fact the developers chose not to indicate the cost associated with using the app upfront. I feel like they wasted my time. I would’ve preferred to decide if I wanted to spend money before they wasted my time. Makes me think less of the content behind the paywall. 

A tip: if you’re going to be sneaky about it, at the very least offer a trial week or month so someone can use it and decide if they like it before committing.

reviews.title: AI Slop App; Not for Adults
reviews.text: Genuinely surprised at how awful this app is. I really have no issue with AI use, but every graphic is generated by AI, and the content itself seemed to be as well. Very annoying practice in the beginning as well where there’s a lengthy quiz to gauge what it is you want to learn, just to at the end of it ask for $60. The worst part, is that the free trial isn’t even available on that page, so the only way to get around it, is by going backward into the quiz and clicking continue again. Some of the reviews are clearly people who assumed they weren’t going to have to pay immediately (which is silly on their behalf as it is pretty clear), but for the time I used it, I feel like I would have been genuinely agitated if I had spent money on it. Do not expect to learn anything from this app if you are an adult; could be useful to a high school student AT BEST.

reviews.title: Garbage don’t buy. The most basic of information you could get from the lead paragraph of a wiki.
reviews.text: Interested by some Instagram ad that said I could learn more about electrical circuits. Then scammed by the SmartyMe  quiz that alluded to a deep understanding of electrical engineering but was the most basic info you learn on a first day of a high school class. Since that subject barely existed I tried giving the app a 2nd, 3rd and 4th chance at learning other subjects… pretty similar experience. Look if you wanna learn take 5 min and google something or watch a video or better yet buy a book… you don’t need this. Make something actually useful and stop trying to scam us with your dollar store startup culture ideas and ai generated targeted ads. I never write reviews and I’m a pretty chill person but the deceptive nature to get me to sign up really frustrated me.

reviews.title: I want to love it - but audio is a disaster
reviews.text: I really want to love this app because the content on ‘Communication Skills’ and ‘Speak Eloquently’ seems genuinely insightful. However, the user experience on my iPhone 16 Pro is a total disaster. The app is plagued by a major audio glitch where playback simply won’t start more than half the time. The only ‘fix’ is to force-close and restart, which leads to a second, equally frustrating issue: progress is never saved. Every time I restart to fix the audio, I’m booted back to the very first lesson. I then have to manually hunt for my topic and scroll until I find where I left off. I’ve paid for a full year and tried every standard remedy—reinstalling the app, checking background refresh, and ensuring I’m not in power saving mode—but nothing works. This is clearly a widespread technical failure that the developers are failing to address. Unless these bugs are fixed immediately, I will be requesting a full refund from Apple as the product is currently unusable.

reviews.title: Feedback on Learning Structure & User Experience
reviews.text:
Hello,

I’m writing to share honest feedback about my experience using Smarty.

I initially discovered the app through Instagram and TikTok ads. The advertising clearly suggested that the app would teach users how to properly use words and sound more confident; with practical examples like “Instead of saying this, say this.” That specific promise is what convinced me to subscribe.

However, the actual experience feels very different. The structure resembles an audiobook rather than an interactive learning platform. While the content may be valuable, the learning process is passive. After completing Section 1, I realized I had already forgotten much of the material because there was no reinforcement, practice, or evaluation.

If this is meant to be a learning application, especially a paid one, there should be interactive components. For example:

	•	A short 10-question quiz at the end of each section.
	•	A requirement to pass the quiz before unlocking the next section.
	•	Practical exercises where users rewrite or complete sentences.
	•	Progress tracking or a points-based system to increase engagement, like gems or tokens.

Without these elements, it feels like I am simply listening to an audiobook breakdown in multiple sections. That is not what the advertising communicated, and it creates a disconnect between expectation and reality.

For comparison, apps like Duolingo make learning engaging by requiring practice, quizzes, and progress milestones. That interactive structure

reviews.title: BEWARE! Misleading Purchasing Process
reviews.text:
After purchasing the app, users are taken through two additional screens promoting paid add-ons. The option to skip these screens is not immediately visible and requires scrolling down to find and select it.

If an add-on is selected, payment is taken from the bank account immediately, without any clear authorisation or confirmation step.

Users are then automatically enrolled in ongoing monthly subscriptions for both the app and the add-ons, which can only be cancelled by logging into their profile and manually cancelling.

Overall, the purchasing process lacks transparency and does not clearly communicate charges or subscription commitments.

I have contacted support to request a refund and have immediately cancelled the subscription

reviews.title: Worth the full monthly cost?
reviews.text: Really good marketing and the content advertised was exactly the personal area I was trying to develop. The content though is very basic, repetitive in places and I would best describe as Ai created generic material. The areas the company push on , small talk was just a small % of the content and the rest is very limited, in my eyes not worth the full subscription.

reviews.title: Rip off
reviews.text: I really wanted to love this app but it seems to be a scam. I don’t believe the reviews given are real. They might be real people but were paid to write them. I downloaded the app, paid for the subscription and couldn’t get access to the content. SmartyMe wasn’t smart enough to figure out how to just give me access to the content or give me a refund. When I tried to cancel, Apple wouldn’t refund my money. I had to go to the card issuer. They wouldn’t refund my money. They said Apple had to and around and around they went until I threatened to cancel the card. I am surprised the app is still available. I hope the same thing doesn’t happen to you.

reviews.title: They trick you into buying. Do not use.
reviews.text:
I downloaded this app thinking it would help me in real life scenarios but it was so AI driven from the start that it was frustrating!! 

I requested a refund and they came back with “our sales are final” however, according to the consumer contracts regulations, I should be able to get a refund within 14 days of purchase.

I’m really disappointed with this app, and hope people take my advice and don’t download it. Look at all the 1 star reviews before purchasing .

reviews.title: Premature Rating Request
reviews.text:
I was really disappointed with the onboarding experience. Before I even finished signing up or using the app, it pushed a rating request in a modal that hid the pricing. On top of that, it asked an excessive number of onboarding questions and then EMAILED the “results” to me instead of showing them INSIDE the app. It felt premature and intrusive.

What bothered me even more was the very first question: “Are you Male or Female?” with no other options. At the very least, there should be a “Prefer not to say” choice. It’s 2026 and on the cusp of AI revolution, so apps should be more thoughtful on user privacy. 

Overall, the experience felt pushy, incomplete, and not user-friendly.

reviews.title: NOT INTERACTIVE
reviews.text:
This app has a series of small lessons on various topics. While some of the information may be useful, much of it is generic or superficial. 

It’s NOT interactive learning AT ALL. Each lesson has the option for the user to read it to themselves or to have an audio track with a robot voice reading it to them. There are no interactive modules or quizzes to reinforce the learning. 

Why do I even need an app for this? I can just look all these things up on the Internet and have it read to me or read it to myself. I canceled my subscription after using the app for about five minutes.

reviews.title: Hustlers
reviews.text: Be careful when buying anything of these guys. They have traps in making you press for upgrades. When I asked about a charge I got a response saying I read the terms and conditions so it’s on me that I got charged for something I had no idea about. They wouldn’t refund instead I got 4 AI generated emails saying they’re not scammers and offering me another package. I would recommend using another platform. And make sure you take your time when going through the steps.

reviews.title: British Lady Voice
reviews.text: I saw this ad on social media and it made me go through a whole screening, asking my preferences like language, what I would like to learn, and also had me choose the voice I would like to hear for learning to personalize my account. I decided to buy the annual subscription. When I started using it I noticed the voice wasn’t the one I originally chose. It was a British lady. It felt like I was learning at Hogwarts. I tried changing the voice and it didn’t even have the option to. I contacted the company and they said they haven’t added that to their app yet and I could not manage any settings. I’m very disappointed in this app. The British lady voice makes me drown out the sound and i cannot learn.

reviews.title: Not Audience-Specific
reviews.text: I find the information in this program very generic and surface-level. For the average educated adult a high school to undergraduate level, 99% of the information contained in this would be very obvious, and it lacks depth. It doesn’t discuss anything cognitive, and it is not fluidly useful. In other words, I cant apply it broadly. I would say the content would be great in a brochure that gives background on a course. For instance “A firm handshake can leave a lasting impression” (very widely known) should be the opener to “and when greeting an authority figure, should be done so like ‘x’, but if greeting someone of the opposite sex should be done from a comfortable distance in a way that allows ‘y’ so as to not come across as ‘z’. If greeting a child, a high five is more likely to leave an impression than a hand shake”. These are just examples but this course sounds like it should be the marketing material for a much better-developed course.

reviews.title: Content Completely Misrepresented
reviews.text: I was targeted with an ad, asking if I wanted to increase my knowledge of film. It asked me about camera angles, post production, and all these other things I’m interested in. I decide to take the plunge and there are literally TWO lessons about Cinema. Both of which are simply the history of cinema from the late 1800’s to the early 1900’s. None of the content was even close to what was promised. Then, once I was done with those two items, there are simply other topics like parenting and other things. I would say less than 1% of their content is related to cinema and it’s nothing you can’t get from a Google search. This app is almost a complete scam. There is content, but it’s not what was promised…not even close. Shame on you guys for tricking people like this. You probably paid to have thousands of people give this app a positive review.

reviews.title: Watch Out for the Billing Trap
reviews.text: I subscribed on the trial, used the service for a day or two, and then stopped using the app altogether. Two months later, I requested cancellation and a refund after seeing the $50  3 month renewal on my account. Customer service sought first to remind me of terms of service (which I hadn’t been updated on) and then offered a $25 refund on a service I had no plans on using for the next 3 months. I was reminded in several emails what I signed up for, and the terms. I reminded customer service that I had received no notice or reminder either of billing or updated terms (which their terms say they will  do—send out an update). Either one would have served as adequate reminder of my subscription, so I could cancel. The spirit of the billing for this service is to charge customers for missing the cancellation deadline on a subscription, essentially getting them to pay for a service they won’t use.

reviews.title: Don’t trust the money back claim, poor quality
reviews.text: The content is worthless, basic, slow and could be replicated with ai in moments with very few prompts. The customer service is fast to reply and did refund something I bought by mistake but the money back guarantee is pointless- you need to be very active on the app to get it yet within a few minutes it was obviously not for me. Clunky interface. Very slow video speed is painful.

reviews.title: Dumbed down too far.
reviews.text:
It’s dumbed down so far that it doesn’t even make sense. It’s like they think you’re too dumb to know or care. 
For instance when talking about how your body might detect the  derivatives involved with walking up a steep slope, onto a flat plane then down again it says if the flat part that you would detect “almost no change at all”. They’ve told you it’s flat, you’d detect no change. This is supposed to be maths! Surely the difference between zero and not zero matters! They somehow think it makes it easier if they fill it with vagaries. Not what I want from a maths course.

reviews.title: Scam
reviews.text:
I have had money taken from my account (random differing amounts) over the last two months. I haven’t been able to login because the email never appeared with the login link. 

This has been at utter sham and scam from the start. I am so annoyed with myself for being stupid enough to sign up. 

Oh and to cancel the subscription l, you have to he logged into the app, which I’ve never been able to login into in the first place. Unbelievably stupid.

reviews.title: Multiple charges for infographic without any notice
reviews.text:
I came across this app on Instagram, and went through the process of creating an account. However, I paid for the 4 week subscription, and little did I know that after clicking on any of the link given, would end up taking money from my account. 

Kindly put more clarifications to this as it comes across as a scam. 

I would gladly appreciate, if the payment for the infographics is cancelled and refunded. I am not interested in the infographics and would like to just stick to the 4 weeks subscription.

reviews.title: AI use and 7th grade writing
reviews.text: The use of AI in ART(!) lessons is horrifying. The irony writes itself. To use an AI generated mockery of the upcoming lesson’s subject instead of the piece of art itself is truly absurd. On top of that, the in-your-face “You’ll never believe what’s next!” writing style is something that I haven’t experienced since I last took a Buzzfeed quiz, in 2016, or maybe even a classmates presentation on beluga whales in middle school. Great idea of an app in theory, but I’ll be requesting getting my money back unfortunately. Edit- emailed to request my refund and I received and email nearly instantly from an AI SUPPORT BOT. I hope the actual humans running this thing have a hot pillow on both sides for the rest of their lives. Disgusting.

reviews.title: DO NOT PURCHASE THE APP
reviews.text:
I’ve been getting charged every month by this company even though I never signed up for any of their services. When I reached out to resolve it, they told me they couldn’t locate any account associated with my name, email, or credit card — yet the charges keep appearing.

What’s even more concerning is that they weren’t able to explain how or why these charges were happening, and I didn’t receive any real help in stopping them. I’ve had to dispute the charges through my credit card company because the business couldn’t provide answers or take responsibility.

If you’re considering using this company, be cautious. Unauthorized billing and lack of support are serious issues, and I hope they fix this for future customers.

reviews.title: No free trial
reviews.text:
Hi! I’m an art student, so I was really excited to try out this app. But after downloading it, I had to fill out a long questionnaire, and at the end, it asked me to pay for a full subscription right away. I was hoping there would be at least a short free trial—maybe three days—to test it out first.

As a student, I can’t afford to spend money on something before I know if I’ll actually like it or learn from it. I ended up deleting the app, which is a shame because it looks really cool. I’d definitely recommend offering a free trial so people like me can experience it before committing!

reviews.title: Don’t waste your money
reviews.text: Wish I’d read the reviews before purchasing the app glad I’ve cancelled my subscription straight away. I’m not quite sure how they’ve managed to get 4.3 stars the positive reviews must be Fake. It’s all AI and the information is so basic it’s ridiculous and boring. I’d like to request my money back but I imagine these companies charge a fairly low fee deliberately so people can’t be bothered to ask for a refund.
